# Independent audit: the strictly convex sector cut-and-fill extension

Read new Section 6 of `candidate 3d1e7a211c24875e` independently, with Sections 1--5 as context. **PASS.** the contributor separately audited the polygon construction and its rational verifier. This audit concerns the arbitrary strictly convex extension, not a general shape reduction.

If points of the added hull stayed away from the chosen ray endpoint P as epsilon tends to zero, strict separating unit normals have a convergent subsequence. Since the hull tends to K and each separating normal must strictly prefer P_epsilon to K, the limiting normal supports K at both P and the limiting added point. Strict convexity makes that exposed face a singleton, a contradiction. The complement of any fixed open neighborhood is closed, so the contradiction applies exactly as stated. No boundary smoothness is needed.

An exterior ball around P_epsilon intersects the cone from P_epsilon to a fixed interior ball on both sides of the source ray in sets of positive area. Consequently the two added capture signatures both occur with positive area. Their union has area tending to zero by the outer-parallel-body containment and continuity from above of finite Lebesgue measure. Choosing a small neighborhood of P places all of it in y>0 and x+y>0, so no additional signatures occur.

The boundary point on the positive diagonal ray lies strictly inside the double-capture quadrant. Every supporting normal there exposes that single point. Sufficiently shallow support caps are therefore localized in the same open quadrant and separated from P. The newly added hull region is eventually disjoint from a fixed such cap, so that cap remains exactly unchanged. Continuity of its parallel cap areas supplies an actual shave of exactly the total added area. The removed region misses all three source lines and has the single double-capture signature.

The total area and the second and third cap volumes are preserved, while the first cap loses exactly the positive left added area. On x=0, every hull point is a convex combination of P_epsilon and an original x=0 point, so the upper endpoint moves exactly epsilon and the lower endpoint does not move. Neither other source line meets either altered region. Thus all section changes and the strict decrease of the selected normalized inverse weight are exact.

The modifications retain a fixed smaller interior ball around the origin. They tend to K: the fill lies in K+epsilon B, and the shallow cap shrinks to its unique exposed point as its area tends to zero. Hence they are genuinely nearby feasible bodies. Componentwise decrease of cap masses preserves both the individual upper bounds and the sorted profile. An initially smallest inverse weight remains smallest because the other normalized weights increase.

The resulting body need not be strictly convex. The conclusion excludes strictly convex bodies as local minima in the full convex-body class, not in a restricted strictly convex class. The proof explicitly fails for a nontrivial supporting face at P, and does not establish a global minimizer, a finite deformation sequence, or a triangle reduction.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
